title: dolphin test suite
description: A test suite for an octo flow: one flow, and the cases that exercise it. It lives beside the flows it tests and is named for them — orders.yaml is tested by orders_test.yaml, the way orders.go is tested by orders_test.go. A case is a debugging run with assertions: the input, the mocks and the spied blocks are the same ones `octo invoke --run-debug-config` takes.

flow.description: The flow under test. Every case in the file calls it.

inputs.description: Named messages the cases share, so the body that means "a vip order" is written once and referred to by name. A case may also write its input inline.

mocks.description: Blocks to stand in for in EVERY case, unless the case overrides the address. This is where "no test in this file ever reaches the payment API" is said once. Keyed by block address.

timeout.description: How long any one case may take. A Go duration. Defaults to 30s, and a case may shorten or lengthen it.

cases.description: The scenarios. Each is one `octo invoke`, in its own process, run with the mocks and spies it asks for.

case.description: One scenario: what to send, what to stand in for, and what should have happened.

name.description: What the case proves, in words. It is what the report, the JUnit XML and a person all identify it by, so it must be unique in the file.
examples: a declined card takes the flow's error path

input.description: What the flow is called with: the name of an entry in `inputs`, or an inline input written out where it is used.

oneOf.description: The name of a shared input.

mocks.description: Blocks to stand in for in this case. An address here REPLACES the file's mock for that block, whole — so a case's mock says exactly what that block will do, without the reader having to hold the file's version in their head too.

spies.description: Blocks to watch, and what each should have seen. Keyed by block address. A block inside a fork branch or a foreach body is crossed once per branch or item, and every crossing is recorded.

timeout.description: How long this case may take. A Go duration, overriding the file's.

skip.description: A reason. The case is reported as skipped and never run — the flow is not called at all.
examples: the upstream contract is still moving

input.description: What the flow is called with. Sources are not started under `invoke`, so nothing populates the message for you.

data.description: The request body, as a structured value rather than a JSON string.

vars.description: Message variables. This is how a case seeds what a source normally would: the http source copies request headers into the variables, so a flow that reads vars needs them supplied here.

expect.description: What the flow should have done. A flow either produces a message, drops it, or fails — so `dropped` and `error` are exclusive with each other AND with the message fields, because a flow that dropped or failed returned no message to check. Omitting `expect` entirely still asserts something: that the flow completed and did not fail.

body.description: The body the flow returned. Compared EXACTLY: a field that appears in the result and not here is a failure, which is what makes the test catch a regression.

vars.description: Variables the flow set. A SUBSET: each key listed must be there and equal, and anything else the flow left behind is ignored — variables are scratch space the engine and the blocks add to. Use `that: ['vars.size() == 2']` when you do want it exact.

that.description: CEL expressions over the result message, every one of which must be true. The same CEL a mock's `when` and every block in the flow uses, over the same variables — body, vars, eventID, correlationID, now. (env is NOT bound: dolphin does not load the config, octo does.) An expression that is not true/false is rejected, rather than read as truthy.

dropped.description: The flow filtered the message out and returned nothing.

error.description: The flow failed, with a message CONTAINING this text. The substring must match: a case expecting "card declined" that passed on any failure would prove the wrong thing.

spyExpect.description: What one watched block should have seen.

count.description: The exact number of times the block was crossed. `0` is an assertion — that the block never ran — which is how a case proves a branch was not taken or an error path not reached.

records.description: The crossings, in order: the first entry is the first time the block was crossed. Asserting on fewer crossings than happened is fine; naming more than happened is a failure.

recordExpect.description: One crossing of a watched block: what went in, and what came out. `output`, `dropped` and `error` are exclusive — a block either returns a message, drops it, or fails. `input` is always available, even for a block that failed: it is captured before the block runs, so a failure still shows what the block was carrying.

dropped.description: The block filtered the message out.

error.description: The block failed, with a message containing this text.

messageExpect.description: What a message should look like.

vars.description: Variables, as a subset: each key listed must be there and equal.

that.description: CEL expressions over the message, every one of which must be true.

mockSpec.description: How one block is stood in for: cases tried in order, and an optional default for a message none of them matched. The block is REPLACED, not wrapped, so its real work — the HTTP call, the LLM, the database write — never happens. Without a default, a message that matches no case fails the block; it does not fall through to the real one, which is gone from the flow.

cases.description: Tried in order; the first whose `when` holds is applied.

mockCase.description: A condition, and what the block should have done when it holds.

when.description: A CEL expression over the message the block RECEIVED — body, vars, env, eventID, correlationID. It is the only expression a mock carries: the outcome below is a literal value, because a mock is a canned response and the dispatch already happened here.

body.description: The body the block returned. A literal value, not an expression.

vars.description: Variables the block set, alongside its body — for the blocks that report through a variable rather than the body, such as an http call setting vars.status. Only valid with a `body`.

error.description: Fail the block with this message, which is how a flow's error path is exercised without arranging for the real block to fail.

drop.description: Filter the message out, as a filter block would.

defaultCase.description: What the block does when no case matched. The same as a case, but with no `when` — it is what runs when nothing else did.

body.description: The body the block returned. A literal value, not an expression.

vars.description: Variables the block set, alongside its body. Only valid with a `body`.

error.description: Fail the block with this message.
